title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A newline eaten by an escape
summary: The shared scan primitive could return a copy with one line fewer, and three detectors number their findings from that copy.

highlights.title: One line short
highlights.description: A backslash at the end of a line inside a string was consumed together with the newline. The copy kept its length and lost a line, so every line number below it moved up by one.

highlights.title: An invariant that is now checked
highlights.description: Length and line count are asserted on a thousand deliberately malformed texts. The property test found a second defect on its own: a trailing backslash made the copy longer than the file.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Blanking a comment or a string never changes the line count of the copy the detectors read.
A backslash at the very end of a file no longer makes that copy longer than the file.
A backslash at the end of a line no longer keeps the string open over the next line.
